name: Whodunit / Detective Mystery
definition: An investigator reconstructs a concealed event by testing clues, suspects, explanations, and the human costs of revealing the truth.
negative_signals: crime used only to start an action chase
diagnostic_questions: Is discovering what happened the central dramatic question?
Can the reader reinterpret earlier evidence after the solution?

neighbors.distinction: Mystery asks who or how; cat-and-mouse asks whether one known opponent can outmaneuver another.
Mystery establishes a hidden truth; legal drama contests which account can be proved.

reader_promises.name: A fair central question
reader_promises.description: Pose a specific unknown and provide interpretable evidence rather than arbitrary concealment.

reader_promises.name: Reinterpretation
reader_promises.description: Make the solution reorganize the meaning of earlier clues, behavior, and omissions.

roles.name: Investigator
roles.description: Pursues the truth through observation, inference, persistence, or personal knowledge.

roles.name: Suspect
roles.description: Offers a plausible motive and a partial account shaped by fear or self-interest.

roles.name: Truth keeper
roles.description: Controls a fact whose disclosure changes the field of explanations.

movements.name: Enigma
movements.description: Present the crime, anomaly, disappearance, or contradiction that demands explanation.

movements.name: Competing inquiry
movements.description: Gather clues while forming and discarding more than one plausible explanation.

movements.name: Crucial inference
movements.description: Connect evidence through an earned insight that changes the active hypothesis.

movements.name: Revelation and reckoning
movements.description: Demonstrate the solution and confront its legal, moral, or relational consequences.

complications.name: Contaminated clue
complications.description: Evidence is genuine but altered, misplaced, or interpreted under a false assumption.

complications.name: Second secret
complications.description: A suspect lies about something important without being guilty of the central crime.

complications.name: Investigator cost
complications.description: Following the evidence threatens the investigator's safety, identity, or loyalty.

twists.name: Method inversion
twists.description: The surprising element is how the act was possible rather than who performed it.

twists.name: Shared causation
twists.description: Several choices jointly produced the crime although responsibility remains legible.

conclusions.name: Demonstrated solution
conclusions.description: The investigator proves a coherent account and exposes the responsible party.

conclusions.name: Truth without justice
conclusions.description: The facts become clear but law, power, or mercy prevents conventional punishment.

conclusions.name: Personal resolution
conclusions.description: The mystery resolves through a private decision whose emotional truth matters most.

variation_axes.question: What grants access to the truth?

subversions: Let the most suspicious behavior protect someone rather than conceal guilt.
Resolve the puzzle while leaving an honest moral ambiguity.
cliches_to_avoid: A solution based on a late unintroduced fact
Clues that exist only because the culprit behaves irrationally
quality_checks: The central solution accounts for the material clues and human behavior.
At least two explanations are genuinely plausible before the key inference.
The revelation changes consequences rather than functioning as exposition alone.

sources.title: MWA University Special Issue
sources.contribution: Discusses suspects, puzzle construction, clue handling, and climactic solution.

sources.title: The Cambridge Companion to Popular Fiction
sources.contribution: Frames crime fiction as a flexible repertoire rather than a homogeneous formula.
